monitoring_fee.⚠️_re_attributed: RE-ATTRIBUTED 2026-08-13 (#1998 tail). This sat under Res. 69-25 as "§5, as amended", which made a 2022 figure read as though the 2025 expansion had set a $2,500 annual administration cap on a $3 billion project. It did not: 69-25 restated §5 and left the fee unchanged. The cap is still worth knowing — it is what the City charges to administer an exemption of any size — but it is 84-22's. Same error class as the designation mis-attribution corrected in #1998, one subsection away, and found the same way: by re-reading a committed instrument instead of reasoning from the file that cites it. ⚠️ The FIRST correction was narrative only — the key stayed nested under 69-25's megaproject block, so a structured consumer still read it as a property of the thirty-year tier. Correcting prose without moving the key is half a fix.

impact_fees.principle: AWS pays the ordinary metered rate for what it uses AND a monthly reserve-capacity impact fee on the UNUSED portion of its reservation, priced at the reserved fraction of the standard rate. the_sequence.note: Every date below is content-verified from the instrument's own passage clause, so the ORDER is solid. What it means is not asserted.

entries.event: A-3219 creates the "Warehouse – Data Center" use, P by right in IIM only
The Planning Commission declines 0-4 to recommend zoning the campus IIM

the_sequence.⚠️_it_names_nothing: A-3219 names no project, no company and no parcel — and a Commission member asked on the record why the category was needed at all (see `deliberation`). Whether it was drafted with this campus in view is [open]. The chronology is a fact; the motive is not in any document read here.

deliberation.the_question: A. Sakhalkar asked for clarification on why the proposed code is specifically calling out data centers when the code currently lists warehouse- small format and large format; noting that a data center should fall under one of those existing uses.
deliberation.the_answer: T. Hurysz replied that the city is being inclusive to different types of uses that may or may not come into the city. Data Centers was not a specific use listed before, but the proposal is to add it. He also noted that the terms for warehouses- small and large format pertains to the literal storage of physical goods and materials. Since a data center stores information, staff feels the distinction needs to be added.
deliberation.note: [verified] This is the only recorded deliberation on why Sidney created a data-center use, and it names no project. The Commission recommended the amendments; Council adopted them six weeks later.

subsequent_amendments.finding: SIDNEY HAS NOT REVISITED THE USE SINCE. The two later zoning-code amendments in the City's Ordinances container — A-3236 (2025-09-22) and A-3255 (2026-02-23) — carry ZERO mentions of data centers between them.
subsequent_amendments.sweep: The negative rests on a full enumeration of the Ordinances container's 2025 and 2026 year folders (49 and 22 documents), of which the zoning-code amendments were opened and read.

cross_site.note: Van Wert wrote "Data Center" into its own code by Ord. 26-05-029 on 2026-05-11, alongside the annexation and zoning of ITS campus the same night. Sidney's definition precedes Van Wert's by about twelve and a half months, and Sidney's definition precedes its own campus zoning by three. TWO SEQUENCES, WRITTEN SEPARATELY. Nothing here supports a claim that either city was responding to the other. See data/extracted/van-wert/council/.
cross_site.⚠️_the_briefed_negative: The research that produced this file was briefed with Van Wert as the network's example and the implication that Sidney had none. That was wrong, and it is recorded here so the next reader does not inherit it.

WHAT A DATA CENTER MAY DO once permitted. The use table grants the use; operating conditions — noise, water, generators, hours — are elsewhere in the code or nowhere, and this ordinance imposes none. ⚠️ Contrast Van Wert, whose conditional-zoning ordinance carried a landscape mound and nothing else: neither city attached operating conditions to a data center.

expansion.what_the_minutes_add: [verified] Community Development Director Barbara Dulworth told Council the expansion "would extend the city Community Reinvestment Area (CRA) boundaries to incorporate the recent annexations, including the 243.092 acres on the north side of Millcreek Road, west of Vandemark Road and the 53.16 acres of land west of Vandemark Road, south of Fair Road." expansion.note: [inference] "The north side of Millcreek Road, west of Vandemark Road" is the same locator the Res. 80-25 recitals use for the Amazon Data Services project site. The minutes do not join the two, and this resolution names no project; recorded as a locator match, not a finding.

megaproject_tier.verbatim: (e) Up to thirty (30) years, and up to one hundred percent (100%) if the commercial or industrial structure is situated on the site of a megaproject and is owned and occupied by a megaproject operator (as such terms are defined in Ohio Revised Code Section 122.17(A)(12)), or is not situated on the site of a megaproject but is owned and occupied by a megaproject supplier that meets the requirements described in Ohio Revised Code Section 122.17(A)(13)(b)
megaproject_tier.ceiling_before_this_resolution: [verified] Res. 84-22 §4 as adopted ran (a) through (d) and stopped at FIFTEEN years / 100% for new commercial and industrial construction. It contains no thirty-year tier and no reference to R.C. 122.17.
megaproject_tier.thresholds_as_stated_to_council: [verified] "large-scale development project meeting specific investment or payroll thresholds, such as at least $1 billion in capital investment or creating $75 million in annual payroll. She noted that the Ohio Department of Development (ODOD) was responsible for certifying megaprojects." — the minutes of this meeting, p. 2. These are STAFF'S characterisation of R.C. 122.17(A)(12); the statute itself is not quoted in the instrument.
megaproject_tier.downstream: [verified] Res. 80-25 (2025-10-27) authorized a CRA Agreement whose exemption is 30 years at 100%. [verified] The minutes of THAT meeting recite this resolution as the authority: "Per the Ohio Revised Code, and the recently adopted revised Sidney City-Wide CRA, property tax abatements for up to 30 years can be approved for megaprojects or megaproject operators."
megaproject_tier.what_is_still_open: [open] Whether the Ohio Department of Development has in fact DESIGNATED this campus a megaproject. The 2025-10-27 minutes say only that the project "meets the requirements to be designated" — eligibility asserted by staff, in the present tense, not a designation stated as made. No ODOD certification is in the corpus.

monitoring_fee.verbatim: SECTION 5. other_sections: [verified] §3 — all residential, commercial and industrial properties in the Expanded Area, consistent with applicable zoning, are eligible.
